sections.name: Dull Bones
sections.card:
Summary: A Dry Bones variant, chartreuse in colour, that throws bones and builds more Dull Bones to help it; it has 1 HP, 2 attack and 1 defense, and turns up commonly in Hooktail Castle.
Weak points: A plain Hammer swing is enough to clear one. Against a crowd, bring a POW Block or Koops's Power Shell. A Dull Bones that has fallen stays down, which sets it apart from Dry Bones.
Tips: Since Build keeps adding Dull Bones to the fight, save the POW Block or Koops's Power Shell for when the field is crowded.
Tips: Besides Hooktail Castle they appear in the Glitz Pit, the Palace of Shadow and the Pit of 100 Trials, and they can drop a Dried Shroom, a Fright Mask or a POW Block.

sections.name: Iron Cleft
sections.card:
Summary: A big blue Cleft made of metal that nothing can pierce. Only two are known: the Iron Adonis Twins, a team you face in the Glitz Pit; each has 6 HP and its Charge hits for 4.
Weak points: Nothing you do damages them, including piercing moves and a perfectly timed Superguard; the only known way to hurt one is Yoshi's Gulp, which uses one Iron Cleft against the other.
Tips: Gulp is a Yoshi Kid move that takes one enemy into his mouth and fires it at a second enemy.

sections.name: Poison Pokey
sections.card:
Summary: A poisonous Pokey with 8 HP and 4 attack that can call in more of its kind; you meet it at Riverside Station and on floors 41 to 49 of the Pit of 100 Trials.
Weak points: Fire works well, since Poison Pokeys are highly susceptible to burning.
Tips: Slam, Body Throw and Bonk do 3, 4 and 5 damage and each can poison you, and its Pull move brings in another Poison Pokey.
Tips: Now and then a beaten Poison Pokey leaves a Tasty Tonic behind, handy for curing any poison it gave you.

sections.name: Magnus von Grapple (Chapter 2 boss)
sections.card:
Summary: The robot Lord Crump operates as the boss of Chapter 2, activated in the Great Tree; it has 30 HP, 2 attack and 1 defense.
Weak points: Its rocket fists count as separate enemies with 2 HP and no defense, and it sends them out once its own HP is down to twenty. A perfectly timed action command on Flurrie's Gale Force always clears them out of the fight.
Tips: As long as a fist is still out, its only attack is a jump followed by rapid stomps that shake the ground: 2 piercing damage to Mario and his partner, though Flurrie floats above it and takes none. Each fist rams a party member for 4 damage.
Tips: Beat both fists and a fresh pair is waiting on its arms two turns later. Each turn after that it uses the stomp, Magnus von Punish, 60% of the time and sends the fists out again 40% of the time. When its own HP hits zero, any fists still in the fight are defeated with it.

sections.name: Doopliss (Chapter 4 boss)
sections.card:
Summary: The Chapter 4 boss, fought in the Creepy Steeple, with 40 HP, 4 attack and no defense.
Weak points: He transforms once his HP is under 20 and then fights with a different set of moves; and if you take him all the way to zero before that point, the transformation still happens and he is left with 10 HP.
Tips: Goombella's Tattle cannot give him a name; it shows five question marks instead.
Tips: Before he transforms his Head Missile does 4 damage; afterwards he uses a Jump that hits twice for 2 and a Hammer swing for 4.

sections.name: Cortez (Chapter 5 boss)
sections.card:
Summary: The pirate skeleton who holds the Sapphire Star in Pirate's Grotto on Keelhaul Key; he has three forms of 20 HP each, 4 attack and 1 defense, and he rises again in a new form when each of the first two falls.
Weak points: In his serpent form the green gem inside his rib cage is the soft spot: hitting the bone pile twice opens the cage, and the gem then has no defense and every attack does 1 extra damage to it.
Tips: In his last form the four weapons fight on their own. A decent-strength attack that reaches every enemy, like a Thunder Rage or Vivian's Fiery Jinx, shuts them down for two turns, and Flurrie's Gale Force can blow them off the stage for good.
Tips: In the first form he swings four weapons and can hit one or both of you each turn, and the rusty hook can poison; at 10 HP or less in the last form he eats half the audience to heal, so a swift finish beats a long fight.

sections.name: Lord Crump (third fight)
sections.card:
Summary: The third time you fight Lord Crump, at Keelhaul Key in Chapter 5, he brings a platoon of X-Nauts: 30 HP a round for two rounds, 3 attack and no defense.
Tips: His only attack is a Body Slam for 3. After round one he heals, and in round two he summons new X-Nauts for the platoon on the turn after the old ones are beaten.

sections.name: Smorg (Chapter 6 boss)
sections.card:
Summary: A huge mass of small Smorgs that attacks on top of the Excess Express in Chapter 6, with 50 HP; unlike every other chapter boss except the final boss, it guards no Crystal Star.
Weak points: Three tentacles, the Smorg Miasmas, ring the main body at the start; defeating them exposes the base of the body and lowers its defense, so take them out first.
Tips: Once it has taken a lot of damage the tentacles reshape into a pincer claw that hits for 10, against 5 for the Tentacle Slap.

sections.name: Magnus von Grapple 2.0 (Chapter 7 boss)
sections.card:
Summary: The upgraded robot Lord Crump drives in the X-Naut Fortress at the end of Chapter 7, with 70 HP, 6 attack and 2 defense; it is the last boss that holds a Crystal Star.
Weak points: Its X-Punch fists are fragile, with 5 HP and no defense, but each hits for 9; Flurrie's Gale Force can blow them away.
Tips: Its main attack is a dive from off-screen that lands on Mario and his partner for 6 damage.
Tips: Its Rapid Fire Cannon pulls in members of the audience, then opens up its front and shoots them at whoever stands first in line: 10 hits of 3 damage each.

sections.name: Gloomtail (Palace of Shadow boss)
sections.card:
Summary: Hooktail's older brother, the dragon who guards the Star Stone in the Palace of Shadow, with 80 HP, 8 attack and 2 defense; he is the stronger of the two siblings.
Weak points: Watch for Charge Up (+8): it is the warning that the Megabreath, worth 16 damage, is about to follow.
Tips: Expect whoever stands in front to be stomped or chomped for 8. The poison from his breath hangs on for at least ten turns. Earthquake hits for 10 and pierces, but Vivian and Flurrie are unaffected by it.
Tips: Defeat him and he spits up a chest with the Star Stone in it; the Palace of Shadow Tower's pedestals will not unlock without that stone.

sections.name: Grodus (Palace of Shadow boss)
sections.card:
Summary: The head of the X-Nauts, fought in the Palace of Shadow, with 50 HP, 7 attack and 1 defense; each Grodus X he has adds 1 to his defense.
Weak points: Four Grodus Xs are needed to raise his protective force field, and destroying just one of them breaks it. Hitting his scepter can stun it, and while it is stunned he cannot attack.
Tips: He casts Thunderbolt (7), Flamethrower (6, burns), Ice Beam (5, freezes) and Clock Beam (stops you), the first three piercing, and he can also counterattack with Payback or turn Dodgy.
Tips: Smoke from his scepter marks a dud move that does no damage.

sections.name: Bonetail (Pit of 100 Trials boss)
sections.card:
Summary: The skeletal dragon at the bottom of the Pit of 100 Trials, with 200 HP, 8 attack and 2 defense, the most HP of any enemy; she is the strongest boss in the game, stronger even than the final boss.
Weak points: When her HP gets low she can recover 20 HP, at most twice, which adds up to 40 HP on top of her 200.
Tips: Her breaths do 8 damage and can freeze (blue), confuse (green, pink in the Switch remake), shrink (purple) or put you to sleep (white); guarding or Shell Shield avoids all of them.
Tips: Besides the breaths and Recover she only has Stomp and Chomp for 8, with none of Gloomtail's earthquake or Megabreath, and once beaten she coughs up the Return Postage badge and cannot be fought again.

sections.name: Star Pieces
sections.card:
Summary: Hidden collectibles: the game has 100 Star Pieces in all. 98 sit out in the world, and the last two are rewards from Chef Shimi and from the waitress on the Excess Express.
Uses: Dazzle, in Rogueport Underground, swaps badges for Star Pieces, and you need all 100 to buy everything he has.
Tips: Dazzle's prices in Star Pieces: Attack FX Y 1, Chill Out 2, Pretty Lucky 3, Happy Flower, Happy Heart and Happy Heart P 4 each, Item Hog 5, Heart Finder and Flower Finder 6 each, Peekaboo 7, Quick Change 8, Flower Saver and Flower Saver P 10 each, Power Plus and Power Plus P 15 each.
Tips: For five coins Merluvlee will predict where they are, and Ms. Mowz can sniff them out with her field ability. Some are buried and need the Super Boots to flip their panel; in the GameCube game the Ultra Hammer cannot do it.

sections.name: Partner ranks
sections.card:
Summary: Ranking up a partner makes its attacks stronger and gives it more HP and a new move. There are two steps, Super Rank and then Ultra Rank, and Merlon in Rogueport does each one for three Shine Sprites.
Uses: Super Rank teaches Goombella Multibonk, Koops Shell Shield, Flurrie Lip Lock, Yoshi Kid Mini-Egg, Bobbery Hold Fast and Ms. Mowz Tease; Ultra Rank teaches Goombella Rally Wink (Mario gets a second turn), Koops Shell Slam, Flurrie Dodgy Fog, Yoshi Kid Stampede, Bobbery Bob-ombast and Ms. Mowz Smooch (heals Mario 10 HP).
Tips: Bobbery has the most HP at each rank (20, 30, then 40), and Koops has the lowest once ranked up (15 at Super, 25 at Ultra).
Tips: The Up Arrow, the key to Ultra Rank, is in Hooktail Castle. Bring Bobbery: in the room where you earlier found the Black Key, he can blast open a crack in the far-right wall, and the secret room behind it has a blue ! Block that reveals the chest. Merlon sends you there after you come back to Rogueport with the Sapphire Star from Keelhaul Key. Hand him the Up Arrow and he lets loose the Ultra Stone, after which he can raise your partners to Ultra Rank.

sections.name: Healing mushrooms
sections.card:
Summary: A Mushroom restores 5 HP; the Super Shroom and the Ultra Shroom are the stronger versions, and since partners have HP now, a Mushroom can heal a partner too.
Uses: When Mario or a partner is knocked out, a Life Shroom brings them back with 10 HP; it is called a Life Mushroom in the Switch remake. A partner uses it by itself the moment its HP runs out, so you cannot hold one back for Mario.
Tips: Northwinds Mart, the Sales Stall, Keelhaul Galleria, Twilight Shop, the souvenir shop and Westside Goods all sell Super Shrooms. Few places sell Ultra Shrooms: 200 coins at the Deepdown Depot, 67 Pianta tokens at the Pianta Parlor (80 in the Switch remake), and now and then 120 coins from Charlieton.
Tips: You get a Life Shroom as the shopping prize at 150 shop points, an enemy may carry one and drop it after it is beaten, and Ms. Mowz can steal it with Kiss Thief.
